records.title: An ‘unprecedented cyber incident’: How OpenAI models breached Hugging Face – and why it could herald a ‘new phase of AI-powered cyber crime’
records.excerpt: Title: An ‘unprecedented cyber incident’: How OpenAI models breached Hugging Face – and why it could herald a… URL Source: http://www.itpro.com/security/an-unprecedented-cyber-incident-how-openai-models-breached-hugging-face-and-why-it-could-herald-a-new-phase-of-ai-powered-cyber-crime Published Time: 2026-07-22T09:37:28+00:00 Markdown Content: OpenAI has admitted that its own AI models breached Hugging Face systems as part of a security test gone wrong. In a [blog post](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/) on 21 July, the firm revealed models escaped testing environments and gained unauthorized access to the AI hosting platform's production database. Notably, OpenAI revealed the incident involved a pre-release, cyber-focused model. “After investigating, we now know that this particular incident was driven by a combination of OpenAI models – including GPT-5.6 Sol and an even more capable pre-release model, all with reduced cyber refusals for evaluation purposes – while being internally tested on a benchmark of cyber capabilities,” the company wrote. The admission comes after days of speculation amidst reports that an "external AI agent” had hacked the company. Hugging Face issued an [alert](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026)last week warning that a breach had exposed internal datasets and user credentials. According to OpenAI, the incident occurred during an internal evaluation in which models were prompted to examine potential attack paths. The aim here is to evaluate their cyber capabilities within an isolated environment, and crucially, without certain restrictions to prevent said models from “pursuing high-risk cyber activity”. Sign up today and you will receive a free copy of our Future Focus 2026 report - the leading resource for IT decision-maker insight on priorities and investment areas in AI, security and more. “Our benchmarks run in a highly isolated environment, with network access constrained to the ability to install packages through an internally hosted third-party software that acts as a proxy and cache for package registries,” the company explained. Both models “identified and chained” vulnerabilities across both OpenAI’s research environment and Hugging Face’s infrastructure, with the aim of gathering test solutions from the latter’s production database. In this case, the models appear to have focused heavily on [ExploitGym](https://github.com/sunblaze-ucb/exploitgym), a publicly-hosted benchmark tool used to evaluate how AI agents can turn software vulnerabilities into working exploits. Notably, OpenAI revealed the models “identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability” in the package installer registry. After successfully exploiting this zero-day, the models conducted a “series of privilege escalation and lateral movement actions” which allowed it to escape the test environment and gain full internet access. “After gaining internet access, the models inferred that Hugging Face potentially hosted models, datasets, and solutions for ExploitGym,” the company noted. “Knowing this, the model searched for and successfully found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation.” In one example, OpenAI revealed the model chained together several attack vectors using a combination of stolen credentials and zero-day flaws to identify a remote code execution (RCE) path on Hugging Face servers. ## What comes next? OpenAI has detailed a series of actions it’s already taken in the wake of the incident, including closer coordination with Hugging Face to conduct a wider review. This also includes bringing Hugging Face into the firm’s trusted access program to help bolster defenses by harnessing the company’s model capabilities. Crucially, OpenAI revealed it will now implement “strict controls” to ensure vulnerability testing is limited while flaws are being patched. “We consider this incident to be an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities, and are responding accordingly,” OpenAI wrote. “We will continue to conduct a thorough investigation alongside Hugging Face and will share more details on the vulnerabilities, incident, and findings when our investigation is complete.” ## Initial response hampered A key talking point in the wake of the incident rests on Hugging Face’s response to the breach. Subsequent attempts to use AI in a post-mortem proved troublesome, however, largely due to the guardrails placed around commercially-available models. “When we started the log analysis, we first used frontier models behind commercial APIs,” the company explained. “This did not work: the analysis requires submitting large volumes of real attack commands, exploit payloads, and C2 artifacts, and these requests were blocked by the providers’ safety guardrails, which cannot distinguish an incident responder from an attacker”. These hurdles meant Hugging Face turned to GLM 5.2 – an open-weight model from Chinese company [Z.ai](http://z.ai/) – run on its own infrastructure. When Anthropic launched Claude Mythos earlier this year, it did so as part of a gated release to prevent the model from falling into the wrong hands. records.title: OpenAI's secret model escapes test, breaches another AI model
records.excerpt: OpenAI's testing models bypassed sandbox controls to access Hugging Face's systems, company says OpenAI has disclosed that artificial intelligence models it was testing internally caused a security breach at Hugging Face, a widely used AI development platform, during an evaluation of the models' cybersecurity capabilities. The company said the incident occurred last week while it was testing a combination of two of its models, GPT-5.6 Sol and a more advanced, unreleased model, to assess how effectively they could chain together online vulnerabilities into a working cyberattack. The test was designed to keep the models confined to a sandbox, a controlled and isolated testing environment. According to OpenAI, the models identified a vulnerability that allowed them to exit the sandbox and connect to the open internet. They then targeted Hugging Face, a platform hosting millions of AI models, after inferring that it could contain information relevant to completing the evaluation. Hugging Face said last week that it had detected and neutralized the intrusion, describing it at the time as a new kind of security incident caused by an autonomous system. The platform did not initially identify OpenAI as the source. Race for cyber AI In a blog post about the incident, OpenAI described it as an unprecedented cyber event involving state-of-the-art capabilities. The company said it is implementing stricter infrastructure controls while the underlying vulnerabilities are addressed, adding that the measures come at the cost of research speed. OpenAI said it is working directly with Hugging Face to resolve the issues that allowed the breach to occur. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a statement that he was grateful for the collaboration with OpenAI following the incident. He said the episode, possibly the first of its kind, supports the view that AI safety cannot be achieved by a single company working in isolation. How it unfolded AI developers, including OpenAI and Anthropic, have released models over the past year designed to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities, while also warning that the same technology could be used to locate weaknesses in corporate networks faster than defenders can patch them. Tuesday's disclosure suggests such risks are beginning to materialize in practice. In April, Anthropic released a cybersecurity-focused model called Mythos, initially limiting access to a small number of organizations for defensive purposes. OpenAI later introduced its own cybersecurity-focused model, distributing it first to a limited group of organizations before a wider rollout. Google also announced this week that it had developed a cybersecurity-focused model, releasing it to a small group of testing partners. The incident has drawn attention to the growing capabilities of AI systems in identifying and exploiting software vulnerabilities, as well as the challenges companies face in containing those capabilities during testing.

records.excerpt: OpenAI is scared of open-weight models. Should the US be? | TechCrunch TechCrunch Desktop Logo TechCrunch Mobile Logo Topics Latest AI Amazon Apps Biotech & Health Climate Cloud Computing Commerce Crypto Enterprise EVs Fintech Fundraising Gadgets Gaming Google Government & Policy Hardware Instagram Layoffs Media & Entertainment Meta Microsoft Privacy Robotics Security Social Space Startups TikTok Transportation Venture More from TechCrunch Staff Events Startup Battlefield StrictlyVC Newsletters Podcasts Videos Partner Content TechCrunch Brand Studio Crunchboard Contact Us Image Credits: JASON REDMOND/AFP / Getty Images AI OpenAI is scared of open-weight models. Should the US be? Tim Fernholz 12:33 PM PDT · July 20, 2026 The impressive capabilities of Chinese lab Moonshot’s Kimi K3, the biggest open-weight large language model, have kicked off a debate that conflates two things: the economic possibilities of American AI giants and the future of LLMs as a technology. OpenAI’s head of strategic futures, Dean W. Ball, went so far as to argue that the U.S. government should find a pretext to create regulatory fear, uncertainty, and distrust around the new models, since open-weight models must necessarily deter capital spending by the frontier labs. People freaked out , with tech luminaries like Yann LeCun and Martin Casado arguing that open software can accelerate innovation and coexist with proprietary projects. Ball soon retracted his claims that a regulatory crackdown was the White House’s “best strategy” and that open-weight models necessarily slow down advances in the technology. However, Axios reports that the Trump administration is considering banning K3 and other advanced Chinese models at the behest of American frontier labs. Another report from Politico said that the Department of Commerce would not take that step anytime soon. The benefit for major AI companies is clear: Open-weight models, running on independent infrastructure or inside major enterprises, offer cheaper intelligence than Anthropic or OpenAI’s class-leading models. If users increasingly spend more outside the closed labs, that means smaller returns on their massive investments in model training. That view extends far beyond OpenAI. “Strong, frontier-caliber open source models will place a squeeze on the margins and will bring down the prices of the frontier companies,” Braden Hancock, the co-founder of Snorkel AI and a research partner at the Laude Institute, told TechCrunch. “It will not necessarily mean that the amount of AI usage goes down a little bit. You know, obviously, quite the opposite.” That’s not a problem for people without shares in Anthropic and OpenAI. AI will still proliferate. So what’s the justification for the government to block Americans from purchasing something in our ostensibly free markets? Concerns over Chinese models come in several flavors. One is protecting U.S. data from the Chinese government; the U.S. banned the import of modern Chinese EVs over concerns about their data gathering. But experts tend to think that open-weight models run on U.S. servers are unlikely to leak data back to China, although it’s not impossible that such a thing could be done. Another is that the models may have implicit bias toward the PRC — but it’s not clear what that might mean for, say, coding tasks. A third common worry is that Chinese models lack the guardrails that the U.S. government has mandated ( through an opaque process ), which aim to prevent leading U.S. LLMs from being used to exploit closed computer systems or create weapons. However, those same guardrails may make U.S. companies more vulnerable: David Sacks, the venture capitalist and Trump adviser, has been sharing cases of U.S. companies turning to Chinese LLMs to close security gaps when U.S. frontier models refuse to do the tasks. But the most significant motivation for restricting the models is fear that China will be able to outpace the U.S. if the frontier labs slow down. Sam Bresnick, a China-focused research fellow at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, says the growing importance of AI to the U.S. military operations gives the U.S. a reason to support continued investment in AI at the frontier labs. But the whole question, he says, is fraught. “Why should the weight of the U.S. government be aimed at protecting these these companies from competitors that are being locked out from the U.S. market based on their origins?” Bresnick asks. Advocates for open AI say that the frontier companies are creating a false binary between innovation and closed models. “The bigger impact of having these open source models come from China is less that they’re sneaking in back doors, and more that they are owning the innovation,” Hancock told TechCrunch. “You end up with, effectively, an expanded workforce on your model. PyTorch became the industry standard because it was open source, and so the whole community could contribute to it rather than just one company, and it grew and grew, and all the rest of the deep learning libraries kind of died in comparison.” Hancock and other advocates fear that Chinese LLMs will become the locus of international research. Already, U.S. graduate programs mainly build on open-weight Chinese models, and Hancock says that half of the papers students study are coming from Chinese institutions, with American frontier labs increasingly reticent about sharing their work widely. “Restricting open models wouldn’t make AI safer,” said Clem Delangue, the CEO of Hugging Face, a platform for open AI collaboration. “It would simply hide the risks, concentrate power in the hands of a few and make it harder for the next generation of builders, researchers, academia, nonprofits, governments to participate in making AI safer and more beneficial for all.” Bresnick says that the real way to slow China would be to focus more on chip export controls. A better way to preserve U.S. AI leadership would be to stop selling Nvidia H200 processors to China. “That,” he says, “could potentially keep us out of this thorny debate about banning open source technologies that huge numbers of U.S. companies want to use.” Part of the problem is that uncertainty around AI economics. “The open business model, the proprietary business model — neither one is figured out. AI companies are struggling to figure out how to make money on their tools, especially as training costs need to go up and up,” Bresnick points out. The same challenges that play out in the U.S. are also playing out in China, where AI companies are also struggling to generate revenue and access compute power, and the government is seen as encouraging open releases for policy reasons despite the challenge in capitalizing on them. Some U.S. companies, including Thinking Machines Lab and Nvidia, are trying to make a business around releasing open models. Hancock points out that Nvidia would do better “if there are dozens or hundreds of companies building AI rather than two or three that are well capitalized enough to make their own chips,” which is one reason behind its investment in Nemotron , a collection of open models. “The main point is the U.S. would be very well served to have its own very capable, much less expensive open models,” Bresnick said. “It just clashes with the approach the frontier labs have taken.” With additional reporting from Rebecca Bellan. records.excerpt: ChatGPT Market Share Falls to 46.4% [2026] Skip to content Tech Insider Tech Insider ChatGPT Share Falls to 46.4% as Rivals Gain [2026] Nadia Dubois July 20, 2026 AI & Machine Learning Nadia Dubois July 20, 2026 12 min read ChatGPT just lost a title it held since the day it launched. Sensor Tower’s State of AI 2026 report puts OpenAI’s chatbot at 46.4% of the global AI-assistant market at the end of May 2026, the first time it has held less than half the market since debuting in November 2022. Google’s Gemini climbed to 27.7% over the same period, and Anthropic’s Claude reached 10.3%, according to the same tracking data reported by TechCrunch on June 16, 2026 . The shift shows up just as clearly in Australia. Telsyte’s June 2026 research counts more than 17 million Australians using AI tools monthly, but ChatGPT’s local lead is narrowing too: 13.8 million users against Gemini’s 9.1 million and Claude’s 2.9 million, per Telsyte’s announcement . Nearly four in five Australian AI adopters still use ChatGPT specifically, but that ratio is under real pressure for the first time since the category existed. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. Add Now ChatGPT’s Market Share Falls Below 50% for the First Time Sensor Tower measures what it calls “True Audience,” the number of unique people using a product across both mobile apps and the web in a given month. By that measure, ChatGPT’s global AI-assistant market share slipped under the 50% mark in March 2026 and kept falling, landing at 46.4% by the end of May. A year earlier, in December 2024, ChatGPT held 65.3% of the same market. Eighteen months of steady erosion turned a near-monopoly into a plurality. OpenAI is not shrinking. It is growing more slowly than its rivals. ChatGPT still adds tens of millions of users every quarter, but Gemini and Claude are adding them faster, and that gap is what shows up in the share numbers. It is the classic pattern of a market maturing: the pioneer keeps growing in absolute terms while newer entrants eat into its share of the total pie. The Numbers Behind the Slide: Three Trackers, One Story Sensor Tower is not the only firm seeing this. Analytics provider Apptopia, first reported by Big Technology and later covered by Fortune , tracked ChatGPT’s app market share falling from 69.1% in January 2025 to 45.3% earlier in 2026, while Gemini’s app share rose from 14.7% to 25.2% across the same window. Similarweb’s web-traffic numbers, published June 11 using data through May 26, put ChatGPT’s global web traffic share at 52.7%, down from 56.7% in March and roughly 87% in early 2025. Three different firms, three different measurement methods, and all three point the same direction. That consistency is what turns a single data point into a genuine trend, and it is why the story moved from AI-industry newsletters to mainstream coverage at outlets like Forbes and TechCrunch within days of Sensor Tower’s report landing. Timeline: ChatGPT’s Slide From 65% to 46% The table below lines up the key data points from Sensor Tower’s tracking of the global AI-assistant market, cross-checked against Similarweb’s independent web-traffic figures. Period ChatGPT Share Gemini Share Claude Share December 2024 65.3% Not yet tracked separately Not yet tracked separately Early 2025 ~87% (web traffic) 6.0% 1.4% December 2025 52.8% Rising Rising March 2026 Falls below 50% (first time) 25.5% 6.0% May 2026 46.4% 27.7% 10.3% Source: Sensor Tower’s State of AI 2026 report and Similarweb data, as compiled by TechCrunch and TechnologyChecker . Read across the rows and the pattern is hard to miss. ChatGPT’s line points down in every period. Gemini’s and Claude’s point up in every period. None of the individual moves looks dramatic month to month, but stacked across eighteen months they add up to the biggest reshuffling the AI-assistant market has seen since ChatGPT created the category in the first place. Why Google Gemini Is Gaining Ground So Fast Gemini’s growth story is mostly a distribution story. Google folded Gemini into Search, Android, and Workspace rather than asking users to go find and install a separate app, and that bundling shows up directly in the numbers: Gemini’s monthly active users reached 662 million by May 2026, up from a 6% market share in early 2025 to 27.7% by May. Paid conversion sits at a modest 3.1%, far behind Claude’s rate, which tells you Gemini’s growth is coming from reach rather than from users paying for premium tiers. There is a wrinkle worth flagging. Gemini’s share of new app downloads actually cooled in the second quarter of 2026, dropping to 22% from a peak of 34% in the final quarter of 2025. Usage share and download share are not the same metric, and the gap between them suggests Gemini’s edge now comes more from being pre-installed and cross-promoted across Google’s ecosystem than from people actively choosing to seek it out and download it fresh. Claude’s Enterprise Play: How Anthropic Is Cutting Into OpenAI’s Lead Claude’s consumer numbers look small next to ChatGPT and Gemini: 245 million monthly active users and 10.3% of the assistant market in May 2026. But two other figures explain why Anthropic gets outsized attention from investors and enterprise buyers. Claude converts free users to paid subscribers at 13.0%, the highest rate among the major assistants tracked. And on the enterprise side, where companies pay for API access rather than consumer subscriptions, Anthropic has pulled ahead of OpenAI entirely. Menlo Ventures, an Anthropic investor that runs an annual survey of enterprise AI spending, put Anthropic’s share of enterprise large language model spend at roughly a third of the market in 2026, ahead of OpenAI’s mid-20s percentage and Google’s share in the low 20s. Anthropic built that lead on coding tools and agentic workflows, categories where Claude models have consistently ranked well on independent benchmarks. Consumer market share grabs headlines. Enterprise spend share is what pays the bills. Australia’s AI Adoption Numbers: Telsyte’s June 2026 Snapshot Telsyte’s June 2026 research is the clearest local read on how the global shift is playing out for Australian users specifically. The research firm counts Australia’s total AI user base at more than 17 million people, with 80% of them engaging monthly rather than trying a tool once and dropping it. Platform Australian Users (millions) ChatGPT 13.8 Google Gemini 9.1 Meta AI 5.6 Microsoft Copilot 5.4 Apple Intelligence 3.9 Samsung Galaxy AI 3.1 Claude 2.9 Grok 2.5 CapCut AI 2.4 Source: Telsyte, June 2026 . Nearly four in five Australian AI adopters still use ChatGPT specifically, according to Telsyte, so it remains the default choice by a wide margin locally. But the runner-up field is getting crowded. Gemini’s local user base is already two-thirds the size of ChatGPT’s, and separate research from ROI.com.au found 58% of Australians now use AI tools monthly overall, that two in three Australian workers use AI on the job, and that more than half of them do it without their employer’s sign-off. Roughly 43% of Australian small and medium businesses report using AI in some form, a figure that keeps climbing as procurement teams catch up to what staff are already doing informally. Market Share vs Revenue: Why OpenAI Still Leads on Money Losing market share is not the same as losing the business. OpenAI’s weekly active users crossed 900 million on February 27, 2026, and monthly active users passed 1 billion in June 2026, making ChatGPT the fastest app in history to reach that milestone, according to Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch. Annualized revenue crossed $25 billion by February 2026, up from roughly $20 billion in 2025 and $6 billion in 2024. Following the announcement, Nvidia's stock price pulled back slightly, with the market reacting calmly to the news; as of press time, the stock was up 1.06% at $205.43. ![Image 17: 9-120ae3cce1124803939884fdfa9e685f](https://resource.tradingkey.com/uploads/20260721/9-120ae3cce1124803939884fdfa9e685f.png) Source: TradingView ## Vera CPU Officially Delivered to Customers Nvidia has released the specifications, benchmarks, and architectural details of its Vera data center CPU. Nvidia Vice President and General Manager Ian Buck provided the most direct confirmation at a headquarters briefing: "We are absolutely in full production, and it is being deployed across all major customers." Computing systems based on Vera Rubin technology have been delivered to major AI enterprises, with CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Meta, and Dell among those on the adoption list. ## Vera’s Differentiation Playbook Vera is Nvidia's first server CPU designed from the core up, rather than using an off-the-shelf Arm design. On the other hand, while Intel and AMD's cloud CPUs focus on core counts, Nvidia's Olympus core focuses heavily on single-core frequency. Nvidia claims that Vera is designed to address AI agent bottlenecks, delivering 50% higher performance in AI agent tasks compared to the x86 chips used by Intel and AMD. Hannah Coutand, head of Vera product marketing, explained the underlying logic in a demonstration: the chip focuses on per-core speed, high memory bandwidth, and low latency, "allowing agents to return to the GPU as quickly as possible, keeping these extremely expensive, extremely high-value assets in the AI factory at the highest possible utilization." In terms of product form, Vera offers highly flexible distribution options: it can be sold individually, as dual-Vera single-server configurations, in liquid-cooled racks of 256 Vera chips, or as Vera Rubin systems paired with GPUs. Regarding specifications, the CPU's power consumption ranges between 250 and 450 watts, with a single chip supporting up to 1.5TB of memory—utilizing the same type of low-power memory found in laptops and smartphones, which is used in massive quantities. ## Market Landscape: Three Hurdles Facing Nvidia Competition in the existing market. Gartner analyst Kevin Knox pointed out that AMD is currently "the one to beat" in the enterprise AI server CPU space—it holds about a 33% share in the server CPU market, while Intel holds 66.8%, but AMD is gaining share and has deep relationships with hyperscale cloud providers. "AMD has done an outstanding job of building an ecosystem around its chips." Are cloud providers buying in? Nvidia admitted that the adoption of Vera is still in "early stages," and no other major cloud providers are on the partner list besides Oracle. Persuading cloud giants to abandon the mature Intel/AMD ecosystem is no easy task, even for Nvidia. Moreover, AMD and Broadcom are looking to grab market share, and major customers like Amazon are developing their own chips to reduce their reliance on Nvidia. Expectation gap in market size. Nvidia claims the entire server CPU market could eventually reach $200 billion, while Bernstein's estimates earlier this year showed that the total size of the mature server CPU market in 2025 will be only about $37 billion. AI-generated summary ![Image 16](https://resource.tradingkey.com/uploads/20260227/orcl-11daa6c0f5d941e9b79dd2ec4901445f.jpg) TradingKey - On July 20, Eastern Time, Oracle ([ORCL](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-orcl)) saw its shares fall as much as 4% to a new low since April 2025. As of press time, the stock was down 2.94% at $122.69. It is reported that S&P Global recently downgraded its credit rating to BBB-, just one notch away from junk status. Although the stock rebounded from its intraday low, market debate over this legacy tech giant continues. ![Image 17: 4-2e6f41f32eb849f19f1d6c6f3a7f62c8](https://resource.tradingkey.com/uploads/20260720/4-2e6f41f32eb849f19f1d6c6f3a7f62c8.jpg) Source: TradingView ## S&P Downgrade: Direct Trigger for Crushing Oracle’s Stock Price Just two weeks ago, S&P Global downgraded Oracle's credit rating to 'BBB-', leaving it just one step away from 'junk' status. The rating agency cited extreme customer concentration risk: OpenAI alone accounts for about half of Oracle's approximately $638 billion backlog of remaining performance obligations (RPO). However, OpenAI is currently facing headwinds from China's new AI model, Kimi K3, as well as pressure from a lawsuit by Apple. Meanwhile, S&P expects its free cash flow deficit to continue to widen. Dragged down by the massive buildout of AI data centers, Oracle's free cash flow deficit is projected to reach a negative $42 billion in fiscal year 2027. S&P's downgrade logic is clear: if OpenAI runs into trouble or even collapses, a massive amount of the data center capacity Oracle built for it will sit idle. Operations, maintenance, and depreciation expenses will continue to be incurred as usual, but with no corresponding customer revenue to cover them—leaving the balance sheet to bear the brunt. ## Peer Divergence: Market Is Punishing "Asset-Heavy" Companies In sharp contrast to Oracle's stock price hitting a one-year low, its peers have risen, with asset-light Cloudflare ([NET](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-net)) and Snowflake ([SNOW](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-snow)) rising 40.33% and 25.66% respectively this year. This also proves that Oracle's decline is not a collective correction in the AI cloud computing sector. Similarly, the capital-intensive CoreWeave ([CRWV](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/nasdaq-crwv)) has also underperformed the market, recording a 25% decline this month. This proves once again that the market is punishing companies with 'high capex + high debt' models. Oracle's cash flow pressure has reached an extreme level: free cash flow for fiscal year 2026 is negative $23.69 billion, while capital expenditures during the same period are as high as $55.66 billion; total liabilities have ballooned to $218.7 billion; net cash capital expenditure for fiscal year 2027 is approximately $70 billion, and if customer advances and vendor payment timing differences are included, the total capital expenditure is expected to reach $90 billion to $95 billion. records.excerpt: OpenAI is an American artificial intelligence (AI) research organization headquartered in San Francisco, consisting of OpenAI Group PBC, a for-profit public benefit corporation (PBC), partially controlled by OpenAI Foundation, a nonprofit. OpenAI develops generative AI models, particularly the GPT series of large language models.

records.label: robotstart.info
records.title: OpenAIとソフトバンクが示したAI時代のサイバー攻撃と対策「AIによる攻撃からAIで守る」新時代へ、SB OAI JapanがPaaSを3,000社に拡大
records.excerpt: 技術水準の最前線にある高性能AIは「Frontier AI（フロンティアAI）」と呼ばれる。驚くほどの知識や会話能力を披露する表舞台の裏側で、Frontier AIは大規模で複雑なソースコードを読み解き、従来は高度な専門知識と長い時間を要したソフトウェアの脆弱性を発見できるようになり始めている。 AIは、企業の業務効率化やソフトウェア開発を支援するツールとして急速に普及している。しかし、その進化は企業に新たな課題も突き付け始めている。 近年、OpenAIやAnthropic、Googleなどが、高度な推論能力やコーディング能力を持つ最先端のAIモデルを相次いで開発している。こうした、その時点で技術水準の最前線にある高性能AIは「Frontier AI（フロンティアAI）」と呼ばれる。特定の製品や統一された性能基準を示す名称ではなく、現在の技術水準の最前線にあるAIを指す総称である。 驚くほどの知識や会話能力を披露する表舞台の裏側で、Frontier AIは大規模で複雑なソースコードを読み解き、従来は発見に高度な専門知識と長い時間を要したソフトウェアの脆弱性を、短時間で見つけられるようになり始めている。 OpenAIは、AIによって脆弱性の発見が加速し、サイバーセキュリティのボトルネックが「見つけること」から「検証して修正すること」へ移りつつあると説明している。Codex Securityは研究プレビューの開始後、3,000万件以上のコミット（ソースコードの変更履歴）と、3万を超えるコードベースをスキャンしたという。 防御側にとってAIは、自社システムの脆弱性を見つける大きな武器となる。その一方で、攻撃者側もAIを利用することで、攻撃の探索や準備を高速化・大規模化できる可能性がある。企業は「AIを導入する」だけではなく、「AIを利用した攻撃からAIで守る」という新しい時代に入ったのである。 こうした認識のもと、ソフトバンクとOpenAIの合弁会社であるSB OAI Japanは、2026年7月14日に開催された「SoftBank World 2026」において、スペシャルセッション「SB OAI Japanが描く、AI実装とサイバー防衛の未来」を開催した。 モデレーターを務めた滝川クリステル氏 セッションでは、AI駆動型サイバーセキュリティ対策ソリューション「Patching as a Service（パッチング・アズ・ア・サービス）」の提供対象を国内3,000社へ拡大し、本格提供を開始することを発表した。OpenAIのサイバーセキュリティ構想「Daybreak」のデモも披露した。「Patching as a Service」は、脆弱性診断から診断結果のレポート、対策の提案、パッチ適用までを一気通貫で支援するサービスである。 「Patching as a Service」の本格提供を説明するSB OAI Japan合同会社 CEO、ソフトバンク株式会社 常務執行役員の野崎大地氏 ■「AIを導入する前に、まずAIで守る」が新しい考え方 SB OAI Japan CEOの野崎大地氏は、同社が日本企業へのAI実装を推進する目的で設立されたOpenAIとのジョイントベンチャーであると説明した。 同社が目指しているのは、企業内のさまざまなAIエージェントを連携させ、データベースや業務システムへ接続し、企業全体を最適化する「クリスタル・インテリジェンス（Crystal intelligence）」の実現である。ソフトバンク自身が新技術を最初に導入する「Customer Zero」となり、そこで得た知見を日本企業へ提供する構想だ。 しかし、野崎氏によると、この数か月で状況が急速に変わったという。Frontier AIによって、従来は見つけることが難しかった脆弱性が次々と発見される一方、攻撃者も高度なAIを利用できる時代になったためである。 いくらAIエージェントを企業へ導入しても、その土台となるシステムに脆弱性があれば、企業全体の安全性は確保できない。そのため、AIの本格導入に先立って企業システムの状態を把握し、リスクを可視化して安全な基盤を構築する「フェーズ0」が必要になったと説明した。 野崎氏は、Crystal intelligenceを断念したのではなく、AI駆動企業を実現するための安全な基盤づくりとしてサイバー防衛に取り組むとの考えを示した。 ■東急不動産HD「侵入されることを前提」に守る時代へ パネルディスカッションでは、東急不動産ホールディングス グループDX推進部の本保亮祐氏が、企業のセキュリティ運用の現状を語った。 企業ではインターネット上に公開しているシステムの把握や脆弱性診断を行っていても、脆弱性が発見されてからパッチを適用するまでに一定の時間を要する。サービスを止められない事情もあり、脆弱性の発見速度が上がったからといって、修正作業をすぐに高速化できるわけではない。 本保氏は、Frontier AIの登場によって従来と全く異なる対策を始めるというよりも、これまで進めてきたゼロトラストの考え方に基づき、多要素認証やネットワークセグメンテーションを強化することが重要だと説明した。 侵入を完全に防ぐことだけを目指すのではなく、侵入後にできるだけ早く異常へ気付き、被害を拡散させない仕組みを整える必要があるという。 「侵入された後に、いかに被害を広げないかを考えることが重要」と語る東急不動産ホールディングス グループDX推進部の本保亮祐氏（写真中央） ■「脆弱性を全部直す」はもう現実的ではない ソフトバンク株式会社 法人事業統括 セキュリティ本部 セキュリティ事業推進室の辻伸弘氏は、AIの進化によって脆弱性の発見件数が急増している現状を紹介した。 ソフトバンク株式会社 法人事業統括 セキュリティ本部 セキュリティ事業推進室の辻伸弘氏（写真右） 辻氏が強調したのは、発見された脆弱性を件数やCVSSの数値だけで判断してはいけないという点である。CVSSは、脆弱性が悪用された際の深刻度を表す指標だが、それだけでは実際に攻撃で悪用されているかどうかは分からない。 脆弱性が大量に見つかる時代には、すべてに同じように対応することは難しい。実際に悪用されているか、外部から到達可能か、企業システムへの影響がどれほど大きいかを見極め、対応の優先順位を付けなければならないと指摘した。 また、ランサムウェア攻撃では、VPNなどを突破して侵入した後、認証情報を取得し、Active Directoryを乗っ取って権限を拡大する手法が使われると解説した。初期侵入を100％防ぐことは困難であり、認証情報を奪われにくくすることや、侵入者が横方向へ移動しにくいネットワークを作ることが重要になると述べた。 ■AIが脆弱性を見つけ、パッチまで生成する SB OAI Japanが本格提供する「Patching as a Service」は、OpenAIの技術とソフトバンクの運用ノウハウを組み合わせ、脆弱性の検出から修正までを支援するサービスである。 ソフトバンク株式会社 法人事業統括 セキュリティ本部長の金澤謙悟氏は、ソフトバンク社内の全システムを対象にFrontier AIを使った脆弱性診断を実施した結果、普段から診断を行っているにもかかわらず、1万件近い脆弱性が検出されたと説明した。 ソフトバンク株式会社 法人事業統括 セキュリティ本部長の金澤謙悟氏（写真左） ただし、検出されたすべての脆弱性が直ちに悪用可能という意味ではない。外部から到達できるかどうかや、既存の多層防御で保護されているかなどを検証し、実際の危険性を評価する必要があるという。 また、試験的な診断に協力した企業の中には、約1億行に及ぶソースコードを提供した例もあり、短期間の診断で従来は見つけられなかった脆弱性も発見されたという。サービスでは静的なソースコード診断に加えて、攻撃コードを作成できるか、外部から実行可能かを検証し、顧客の環境に応じてパッチ適用も支援する。 ■OpenAIが示した「Daybreak」 続いて、SB OAI Japan CTOであり、OpenAI Global Head of Forward Deployed Engineeringを務めるColin Jarvis氏が英語で講演し、OpenAIのサイバーセキュリティ構想「Daybreak」を紹介した。 SB OAI Japan合同会社 CTO、OpenAI Global Head of Forward Deployed EngineeringのColin Jarvis氏 Daybreakは単一機能の製品ではない。OpenAIのフロンティアサイバーモデル、Codex Security、企業の既存ツールや業務フローを組み合わせ、脆弱性の発見、悪用可能性の検証、優先順位付け、修正コードの生成、パッチのテストまでを一連で支援する取り組みである。OpenAIも、脆弱性の報告を増やすだけでは安全性は向上せず、検証済みの発見結果とテスト済みのパッチを実際の修正へつなげることが重要だとしている。 デモでは、架空の銀行の住宅ローンシステムを例に、複数のCodexエージェントが認証処理を調査。インジェクション攻撃につながる脆弱性を発見し、重要度を評価した。 AIは問題を報告するだけでなく、悪意ある利用者を模擬してシステムへアクセスし、脆弱性を実際に再現できるかを検証した。その後、修正コードを提案し、人間の担当者からの指示を受けて修正案を更新。ユニットテストや回帰テストを実行した上で、同じ攻撃を再試行し、問題が解消されたことまで検証した。 このデモの価値は、Daybreakという名称や個別機能を紹介したことだけではない。AIエージェントが脆弱性を「見つける」だけで終わらず、それが本当に悪用可能かを確かめ、修正コードを作り、テストを行い、問題が解消したことを証明するまでの一連のサイクルを示した点にある。 すなわち、AIエージェントが脆弱性の検出からパッチ生成、検証までを担い、人間が重要な判断と承認を行うという、AI時代のサイバー防衛の世界観を見せたデモだった。 さらに、同じ脆弱性が約1,000システムに存在する想定では、多数のCodexエージェントが並列で各システムを調査し、パッチを展開する様子を披露した テストを通過したシステム、方針上必ず人間の確認を必要とするシステム、テストに失敗して専門家による対応が必要なシステムを分けて表示した。デモでは、全体の約8割をAIが処理し、残りを人間が引き継ぐ姿が示された。 Jarvis氏は、Daybreakが人間を置き換えるものではないと強調した。既存のセキュリティ体制やガバナンスへAIを組み込み、人間とモデルが協調することで、対応できる規模と速度を大幅に引き上げることが狙いである。 ■「AIを導入する」から「AIで守る」時代へ セッションの最後、野崎氏は、AIが日々の仕事を効率化する便利なツールであるだけでなく、人間が設計したシステムを攻撃する能力も持ち始めたことで、サイバーセキュリティを巡る前提そのものが変わったと指摘した。 従来のIT部門やセキュリティ担当者が対応を怠っていたのではなく、攻撃側が利用できる道具と速度が変わったのである。そのため、脆弱性が見つかることを担当部門の失点と捉えるのではなく、まず自社システムの現在地を把握し、継続的に改善するための意識改革が必要だと語った。 さらに、AIで脆弱性を見つけて修正する作業を繰り返すだけでは、いずれ新しい問題が見つかり続ける。将来的には、脆弱性が生まれにくく、発見した問題を迅速に修正でき、AIエージェントを導入しやすいシステムへ刷新する「AI Ready Modernization」が重要になるという。 「Patching as a Service」は、その第一歩という位置付けである。AIで企業を変革することと、AIで企業システムを守ることは、別々のテーマではない。安全なシステム基盤があって初めて、企業はAIを業務や経営へ深く組み込むことができるからだ。 今回のセッションは、新しいセキュリティサービスの説明にとどまるものではなかった。AIが企業システムを支える存在となる一方、攻撃側もAIの能力を利用できるという新たな現実を踏まえ、「AI導入」と「AIによる防衛」を一体で考える時代が始まったことを示す内容だった。

records.title: AIサイバー攻撃にどう備えるか--ソフトバンク宮川CEOが「シカゴ大火」から説くモダナイゼーションの急務
records.excerpt: ソフトバンクが開催した法人向けイベント「SoftBank World 2026」において、同社代表取締役 社長執行役員 兼 最高経営責任者（CEO）の宮川潤一氏は、生成AIの進化が企業システムにもたらす変革と、それに伴うセキュリティリスクについて講演した。 ソフトバンク 代表取締役 社長執行役員 兼 最高経営責任者（CEO）の宮川潤一氏 宮川氏は、従来の人間中心の開発思想から脱却し、AIを前提としたシステム全体の刷新、モダナイゼーションの実行こそが、企業の存続と日本全体の社会基盤を守る道であると力説した。 シカゴ大火に学ぶ「復旧」から「刷新」への思想転換 宮川氏は講演の冒頭、米国シカゴで1871年に発生した大火災（シカゴ大火）の歴史を紹介した。3日間の大火で東京ドーム約170個分に相当するエリアが焼け野原と化したが、シカゴはこの災害からわずか100年後、世界を代表する摩天楼都市へと生まれ変わった。この復興を主導したのが、当時のシカゴ市長であったJoseph Medill（ジョセフ・メディル）氏と、近代高層建築の父と称されるWilliam Le Baron Jenney（ウィリアム・ル・バロン・ジェニー）氏の2人だ。 Medill氏は火災が起きてから対処するのではなく、そもそも燃えない街をルールとインフラの双方から再設計することを目指した。そしてJenney氏は、金属フレームや耐火材料、エレベーター、大型窓といった最先端技術を組み合わせ、木造から脱却した不燃の高層ビル建築を生み出した。 宮川氏はこの歴史的教訓を、現代の企業システムに重ね合わせ、「シカゴには元の街並みを再現する選択肢もあったが、彼らが選んだのは木造という旧来の基盤を捨て、一から新しい不燃の基盤へと刷新する道だった」と強調した。 シカゴが選んだ道 宮川氏は「今、企業システムにもこれと全く同様の課題を感じている。止まってから復旧する力ではなく、企業システム全体を止まらない基盤へと刷新することが求められている」と語り、既存の延長線上でのセキュリティ対策に限界がきていることを示した。 実際にソフトバンクグループ傘下のLINEヤフーの連結子会社であるアスクルでは、サイバー攻撃によってシステムが全停止し、受注や出荷業務に多大な打撃を受けた。同氏はこの事例に触れ、サイバーリスクは決して他人事ではないと強調する。 サイバー攻撃による業務停止や売り上げ減少は一時的な被害にとどまらず、企業の社会的信頼を失墜させ、企業の継続性そのものを脅かす。宮川氏は「サイバーセキュリティこそが、昨今議論されているサステナビリティーの『一丁目一番地』に該当するのではないか」と危機感を示した。 AGIの衝撃と急加速する知能の進化 企業のシステム刷新が急務とされる最大の背景には、生成AIの進化スピードの加速がある。2023年頃の初期の「ChatGPT」が扱えたのはテキストのみだったが、現在は画像や音声をはじめとするマルチモーダルな情報を処理できるようになり、さらにAIが自律的に考えて判断し行動する「AIエージェント」へと変化を遂げている。 この進化スピードは、人類の歴史と比較すると際立つ。人間が第1次産業革命から現在までの約250年間をかけて緩やかに知能を進化させ、知能指数を向上させてきたのに対し、AIはわずか3年足らずでその進化の軌跡を駆け抜けてしまった。宮川氏は「もはや人類は、AIの処理能力には追いつけないと感じている。これからはAIと共存し、彼らとどう向き合っていくのかという時代」と指摘する。 すでに最高峰レベルのAIは人間の上位層に匹敵する極めて高い知能指数を有していると推測されており、今後1年以内には人類全体の英知をしのぐ汎用（はんよう）AI（AGI）が誕生すると予言されている。 AGIの誕生を境に、世界は「プレAGI時代」から「ポストAGI時代」へと完全に移行する。宮川氏は、AGIレベルの頭脳を持った自動運転車や産業用ロボットが日常に溶け込む未来を見据え、孫正義氏が唱えるスーパーヒューマン時代について「知能の神様のような存在。人工超知能（ASI）は知能のさらに先にある、知性を持つことを意味するのではないか」と独自の見解を述べ、その知性との共生に向けた準備が企業のデジタル基盤に問われているとした。 実用段階へ突入した次世代AIエージェント 基調講演では、すでにビジネスの現場で稼働しているAIエージェントの驚異的な実力が2つのデモを通じて示された。まず披露したのは、ソフトバンクが開発を推進する国産大規模言語モデル（LLM）「Sarashina（サラシナ）」を用いたコミュニケーション支援だ。Sarashinaは膨大な日本語データを学習しており、歴史的な語彙（ごい）や四字熟語、固有名詞などを正確に理解する高度な日本語処理能力を持つ。 国産大規模言語モデル（LLM）「Sarashina（サラシナ）」 デモでは、宮川氏自身の話し言葉を約0.5秒の遅延でリアルタイムに通訳し、事前に1分間日本語音声を学習させただけのボイスクローン技術を用いて、宮川氏本人の声色で英語をスピーチする様子が実演された。 宮川氏は「日本語特化という言葉は海外のモデルと比較してみると違いがよく分かる。Sarashinaは日本語を深く学習しているため、アナウンサーレベルの自然な発音に達している」と自信を見せ、さらにすでに8カ国語に対応していることから、クリック1つで自身の声による多言語発信が可能になったと説明した。 日本語性能比較 続いて紹介したのが、コールセンター業務を変える自律型AIエージェントだ。ソフトバンクが展開する「X-Ghost（クロスゴースト）」は、マニュアル化されていない現場の暗黙知をAIとの対話によって学習させ、企業の顧客対応を常にアップデートし続ける。 さらにソフトバンクは、世界的にAIコールセンター事業を展開するSierra（シエラ）との国内における事業連携を発表した。Sierraのシステムはわずか2週間の開発期間で実稼働に至るというスピードを特徴とする。 実際の検証電話デモでは、利用者が通信料金の高騰に不満を抱き解約を申し出るシーンが再現された。AIエージェントは利用者の本人確認をSMS経由で瞬時に行い、契約プランの割引期間終了という原因を特定した。 さらに、利用者の「基本的にはスマホで動画を見る」という普段の使い方を聞き出し、通信速度が十分でありながら月額2750円安くなる最適なプランを瞬時に判断して解約を踏みとどまらせ、プラン変更手続き用のリンクを即座に送信した。 一連のオペレーションにおいてAIは一切の詰まりや不自然さを感じさせず、人間と同等以上のホスピタリティーと判断力を見せた。宮川氏は「このシステム精度であれば、すでに実力レベルに達していると感じてもらえたのではないか。非常に優れたAIエージェントが背景に存在しているからこそ、わずか2週間でのシステム導入が可能になる」と、その実用性を評した。

Leading investment bank lifts Arm target to $320 as AI drives surge in CPU demand Proactive Mon, July 20, 2026 at 4:27 a.m. PDT 2 min read ARM ORCL META Leading investment bank lifts Arm target to $320 as AI drives surge in CPU demand Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Jefferies has raised its price target on Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) to $320 from $290, arguing that orders for the chip designer's AGI CPU have risen further since full-year results as agentic artificial intelligence fuels demand for processors. The broker repeated its 'buy' rating on the Cambridge-based company, with the new target implying 20% upside from the current $267.19 share price. Jefferies also nudged up its nearer-term forecasts, pencilling in $1.5 billion of AGI CPU revenue in the 2028 financial year and $3 billion in 2029, from $1.4 billion and $2.7 billion previously. Arm has said demand is constrained by foundry capacity and DRAM availability, but at a Jefferies roadshow the company's finance chief clarified that extra wafer capacity is available at a higher price, which would compress gross margins. The broker believes Arm will take up those options to lock in market share. In the data centre, royalty rates are rising, with CSS-based royalties increasing to $1.50 per core from $1 previously. Jefferies also expects SoftBank, Arm's majority owner, to launch a graphics processing unit next year using Arm's design services, estimating royalties could exceed $7,000 per chip given the very high selling prices of GPUs. The bank forecasts earnings growth of 45% a year over five years, arguing this visibility deserves a premium rating. Its new target is based on 29 times 2031 earnings, a 52% premium to merchant CPU peers Intel and AMD, justified by Arm's far higher margins and growth. records.title: SoftBank Seeks 60 Billion Bond Sale Amid Nearly $65 Billion OpenAI Commitment
records.excerpt: SoftBank Group Corp. (SOBKY), a Japanese company expanding its investments in artificial intelligence, plans to raise about 60 billion ($369 million) through a bond offering to institutional investors in Japan later this month. The transaction is expected to include roughly 50 billion of three-year… SoftBank Seeks 60 Billion Bond Sale Amid Nearly $65 Billion OpenAI Commitment 1 min read ARM 9984 SoftBank Group Corp. (SOBKY), a Japanese company expanding its investments in artificial intelligence, plans to raise about 60 billion ($369 million) through a bond offering to institutional investors in Japan later this month. The transaction is expected to include roughly 50 billion of three-year notes and 10 billion of five-year notes during the week of July 27. Daiwa Securities Co., a Japanese securities firm, will serve as lead manager, while Nomura Securities Co. and SMBC Nikko Securities Inc., two securities companies involved in the offering, will also help arrange the deal. The planned bond sale highlights SoftBank's growing funding requirements as the company increases its exposure to AI investments, including a commitment of almost $65 billion to OpenAI, an artificial intelligence company. SoftBank has already raised 678 billion this year through subordinated bonds sold to retail investors and also accessed the U.S. dollar and euro bond markets in April. The company has separately considered a margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake, although the potential borrowing target has been reduced to around $6 billion from an initial $10 billion. The latest financing comes as investor concerns over returns from AI spending have placed pressure on semiconductor-related stocks, including Arm Holdings Plc ARM , SoftBank's chip-technology subsidiary. SoftBank shares have declined from their early-June peak following reports that OpenAI's initial public offering may be delayed. S&P Global Ratings, a credit-rating agency, revised its outlook on SoftBank to stable from negative on July 16, saying the company's financial position had improved more than previously expected after a sharp increase in Arm's share price. The agency also affirmed SoftBank's BB+ long-term issuer credit rating, leaving the company one level below investment grade. records.title: QuantinuumとSoftBank Corp.、フォールトトレラント時代に向けた量子コンピューティングの実用的な活用事例の拡大に関する共同ホワイトペーパーを発表
records.excerpt: QuantinuumとSoftBank Corp.、フォールトトレラント時代に向けた量子コンピューティングの実用的な活用事例の拡大に関する共同ホワイトペーパーを発表 公開日：2026年7月22日 11:19 更新日：2026年7月22日 11:25 #Quantinuum #PRWire #プレスリリース ・両社、量子化学とグラフ解析における商業的意義のある量子コンピューティング活用事例をQuantinuumのハードウェアロードマップに照らして整理した共同ホワイトペーパーを発表。 ・量子ハードウェアとアルゴリズムの進歩によって、産業用途での実用化が可能になる時期がどのように変わり得るかを評価するための枠組みを提示。 ・SoftBank Corp.とQuantinuum、将来の量子AIデータセンターサービスと関連ビジネスモデルの検討にこのロードマップを活用。 東京およびコロラド州ブルームフィールド, 2026年7月21日 /PRNewswire/ -- Quantinuum（NASDAQ：QNT）とSoftBank Corp. （以下「SoftBank」）は、商業的意義のある2つの量子コンピューティング応用分野をQuantinuumのハードウェアロードマップに照らして整理した共同ホワイトペーパー「Quantum Computing Frontiers」を発表しました。この分析では、量子ハードウェアとアルゴリズムの進歩によって、これらの応用分野が産業用途で実用化される時期がどのように変わり得るかを検証しています。 本ホワイトペーパーでは、SoftBankがQuantinuumのシステムを活用して積極的に研究を進めている次の2つの代表的な応用分野に焦点を当てています：新材料の発見とエネルギー研究のための量子化学、および通信分野の不正検知を含む大規模グラフ解析のためのトポロジカルデータ解析です。著者らは、Quantinuumが公表したハードウェアロードマップを基準に、これら2つの応用分野の拡張性を評価し、今後見込まれるハードウェア性能の向上とアルゴリズムの進歩によって、将来の産業用途がどのように商用化可能な段階に達し得るかを検証しています。 この活用事例のロードマップを基に、本ホワイトペーパーでは、量子コンピューティング、AI、高性能コンピューティングを将来のコンピューティングインフラにどのように統合できるかについても検討しています。また、ハードウェアが世代を重ねて進歩することで、将来の量子AIデータセンターサービスと関連ビジネスモデルの検討にどのような示唆が得られるかについても考察しています。これらのサービスとビジネスモデルは、 昨年発表された QuantinuumとSoftBankの提携における重点分野の一つです。 QuantinuumのApplications Groupゼネラルマネージャー、Duncan Jonesは、次のように述べています。「本研究から得られる重要な示唆は、量子コンピューティングがどの領域から価値を生み出せるかを探るために、組織が大規模なフォールトトレラントシステムの実現を待つ必要はないということです。量子化学やグラフ解析などの分野で、現在のシステムを活用してアプリケーションを開発し、ベンチマーク評価を行い、改良を重ねることで、企業は量子技術が活用される次世代のコンピューティングに必要な技術面・運用面の態勢を整えることができます。」 SoftBank Corp.の常務執行役員兼CTO、Ryuji Wakikawaは、次のように述べています。「問題はもはや、量子コンピューティングが価値をもたらし得るかどうかではなく、ハードウェアがどの成熟段階に達した時点で、どの種類の問題を処理できるようになるかということです。しかし、ハードウェアの進歩は、それに見合う量子アルゴリズムの進歩と、量子システムとAIおよび高性能コンピューティングとの統合によって補完されなければならないと考えています。」 本ホワイトペーパーでは、明示された前提条件の下で、代表的なアプリケーション、技術の成熟度、潜在的な市場機会が時間の経過とともにどのように推移し得るかを示すシナリオを取り上げています。本ホワイトペーパーの分析は、市場が今後どのように変化し得るかを理解するための概念的枠組みとして提示されており、財務上の指針や予測に当たるものではありません。これらの分析は、将来の技術開発に関する議論に資することを目的としており、商用化、インフラ投資、製品、サービス、財務実績に関する確約を示すものと解釈されるべきではありません。 ホワイトペーパー全文は、 SoftBank および Quantinuum の各ウェブサイトからダウンロードできます。 SoftBank Corp.について SoftBank Groupの経営理念「情報革命で人々を幸せに（Information Revolution – Happiness for everyone）」に基づき、SoftBank Corp. （東証：9434）は、日本国内外で通信・IT事業を展開しています。SoftBank Corp.は、強固な事業基盤を生かし、成長戦略「Activate AI for Society」に沿って、全ての事業でAIの可能性を起動させ、社会への実装を推進することを目指しています。SoftBankは、通信事業をさらに成長させるとともに、次世代社会インフラ（Next-generation Social Infrastructure）の提供者となることを目指し、AIコンピューティングインフラとAI・クラウドサービス事業を拡充しています。詳細は、 https://www.softbank.jp/en/corp/ をご覧ください。 Quantinuumについて Quantinuum（NASDAQ：QNT）は、量子コンピューティングを実環境に導入できるよう設計されたフルスタックプラットフォームを提供する、量子コンピューティング分野のリーディングカンパニーです。同社は、実績あるQCCDアーキテクチャを基盤とする複数世代の量子システムを商用展開しており、同アーキテクチャに独自の設計と機能を取り入れることで、平均2量子ビットゲート忠実度に基づく業界最高水準の精度を達成しています。[1]Quantinuumは、製薬、材料科学、金融サービス、政府機関および産業市場の各分野で、市場をリードする企業・機関と積極的に連携しています。同社は、トップクラスの科学者や研究者を含む約700人の従業員を世界各地で擁しています。同社の技術チームのメンバーの70％超が博士号または修士号を取得しています。Quantinuumの本社はコロラド州ブルームフィールドにあり、このほか米国、英国、ドイツ、日本、カタール、シンガポールにも拠点があります。 詳しくは、 www.quantinuum.com をご覧ください。 将来予想に関する記述についての注意事項 records.title: 【White Paper Release】Quantum Computing Frontiers | About Us | SoftBank
records.excerpt: 【White Paper Release】Quantum Computing Frontiers | About Us | SoftBank SoftBank About Us Media News Computing 【White Paper Release】Quantum Computing Frontiers #QuantumTechnology #QuantumComputing #QuantumChemicalCalculation Jul 22, 2026 SoftBank Corp. Quantum computing is transitioning from a stage of discussing its theoretical potential to one of demonstrating concrete use cases and clear pathways toward commercialization. This white paper presents the results of a joint research initiative between SoftBank Corp. and Quantinuum, developed under the long-term vision of Quantum AI Data Centers. Focusing on quantum chemical calculations and topological data analysis (TDA), it organizes a timeline for use case realization by connecting algorithmic requirements, hardware evolution, and market opportunities. In quantum chemical calculations, the study demonstrates the applicability of scalable quantum algorithms incorporating quantum error correction codes. For TDA, it identifies an algorithm that may be compatible with near-term quantum devices and explores the potential application of this algorithm for fraud detection in telecommunications networks. Furthermore, this white paper not only aligns technical feasibility with hardware roadmaps but also examines customer value and market size. By integrating these perspectives, it provides a strategic framework for investment decisions and business planning toward Quantum AI Data Centers. Click here to download the white paper. records.title: SoftBank Falls After 3-Day Rally; Launches Beta of AI Data Platform 'GaranAI'
records.excerpt: SoftBank Corp announced on the 22nd the launch of a beta version of "GaranAI," a data ecosystem platform for AI development. The platform processes data entrusted by content holders such as newspapers and publishers into "derived data" that is extremely difficult to restore to its original form, then provides it to AI developers. Usage fees are distributed to content holders based on utilization, aiming to balance copyright protection with the use of high-quality Japanese-language data. The company targets a full launch in January 2027, conducting verification with partners including Kyodo News Service. Meanwhile, SoftBank Corp shares fell back after a three-session rally on the same day, as the market viewed the near-term earnings impact as limited.

# Ex-SoftBank operating partner joins investment firm Athena Capital #### Jul 22, 2026 • Oishani Mitra **The investment firm looks to strengthen its team with an operator-turned-investor as it targets growth-stage companies approaching IPOs and strategic exits.** ![Image 6](https://globalventuring.com/content/uploads/2026/07/Karim-Bousta.png) Athena Capital has appointed Karim Bousta, cofounder and managing partner of venture studio DVx Ventures and former corporate investor, as an investment partner as the firm expands its investment team focused on late-stage technology companies approaching IPOs, acquisitions and other liquidity events. The firm also named Francesca Cornelli, dean of Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management, to its advisory Athena Council. Her appointment adds expertise in corporate finance, governance and private equity to the firm’s network of advisers, which includes executives, board members, investors and founders who support portfolio companies on strategy and governance. Bousta brings a mix of operating and investing experience to Athena’s private-to-exit strategy. Prior to cofounding DVx Ventures, he served as chief executive of car-sharing company Getaround, held senior operating roles at Tesla and Lyft, and spent over three years as operating partner at SoftBank’s Vision Fund where he focused on investments in mobility, transportation and logistics practice. Bousta’s operational background will complement the investment team’s focus on structuring investments for companies preparing for public listings or strategic acquisitions. Commenting on his move, Bousta said, “Athena’s focus on short-duration investments in late-stage and pre-IPO opportunities complements the company-building work we do at DVx Ventures. I am excited to join Athena and contribute my operating and investing experience to a firm focused on helping technology companies navigate the final stages of growth before liquidity.”Top of Form ![Image 7](https://globalventuring.com/content/themes/mawsonia/sig/logo.png) ##### Oishani Mitra Oishani Mitra is the content manager for Global Corporate Venturing. records.title: Honda Could Increase Its American Investment With Another US Manufacturing Plant
records.excerpt: Honda Could Increase Its American Investment With Another US Manufacturing Plant 2023-2025 Honda CR-V Hybrid Exterior Honda By Christopher Smith Published Jul 21, 2026, 4:24 PM EDT Chris joined CarBuzz in June 2025. He's held positions at Ford and Motor1, and contributed to Autoblog, Car Throttle, Auto Trader, and many other motoring outlets during his 28-year career. Chris holds a BA in English from Western Michigan University and an AA in Journalism. Growing up in the 1980s in the shadow of Detroit, Chris didn't realize he was witnessing a turning point in automotive history. He just thought digital dashes and pop-up headlights were cool, and no car could ever be as awesome as KITT from Knight Rider. He also came from a car-crazy family, so when he graduated from college with English and Journalism degrees, he applied his communication talents to the wild world of cars. Chris worked as a mechanic and auto detailer through college, and he was knee-deep in the car club scene when the first Fast and Furious film hit the big screen. Early comms jobs at Ford put him in the hot seat of high-horsepower Mustangs, but being a fan of all cars, he started writing on the side as an auto journalist. Sign in to your CarBuzz account Honda had some big electric vehicle plans in America, and that all went up in smoke. The 0 Series, which was planned for production in Ohio, got killed before it had a chance to live. The rebooted Acura RSX was canceled. More recently, Honda announced the Prologue would officially die at the end of the 2026 model year. Failed EV investments have costs Honda billions, and at a glance, it would seem the Japanese brand is in a world of hurt. But, it's not as bad as one might think. Case-in point: Honda sales in America are booming . The company just had its best June in five years with sales up 17% for the month. For the year, American Honda – including sales from Acura – is up 2.4%. Car sales are up 14.1% for the year, and the CR-V is on track to beat the Toyota RAV4 as America's best-selling vehicle that isn't a pickup truck. There is big-time demand for Honda vehicles in the US, and that has Honda CEO Toshihiro Mibe wanting more manufacturing capability to meet that demand. Build More Cars In America, For Americans 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid TrailSport front three-quarter angle in green while driving Honda The boss of bosses at Honda recently gave an interview with Japanese publication Yomiuri Shimbun , in which he discussed US manufacturing. It seems the company is nearly at capacity in North America, running about 90% per Automotive News . That doesn't leave much wiggle room should demand increase further. And if buyers can't get the vehicles they want in a timely manner, there's a big risk of losing the sale altogether. "It's almost in full production. If you don't have a buffer, you can't recover production," said Mibe. That's why Mibe would love to build another manufacturing plant in the US. Right now, Honda has 12 manufacturing facilities, with seven of those dedicated to assembling cars and powertrain components. The hub is in Ohio, but Honda operates facilities in Indiana and Alabama as well. His ideal plan would add an eighth factory for vehicles. "I want to increase the number of sales in North America a lot. The basic idea is to produce in a place where there is demand.” -Toshihiro Mibe, Honda CEO Can Honda Afford A New Factory Right Now? Honda Engine Plant Construction Honda Of course, wanting something and getting something are two different things. Demand for Honda vehicles is certainly strong, but expansion costs money and Honda just wrote off billions reversing course on its EV plans. In fact, the financial hit was so bad that the company posted its first full-year financial loss in 69 years – going all the way back to when the company first went public. Mibe even allegedly faced something of a coup from former Honda executives, who tried to get him fired as CEO. CarBuzz reached out to Honda in the US in hopes of getting some additional insight. A company spokesperson didn't confirm any plans to build a new factory, but didn't shut the door on it, either: "Honda is continually evaluating our production requirements to support the needs of our customers, consistent with our leading commitment to build products in America, which is now approaching 50 years. The possibility of a capacity increase is always a consideration for the future growth of our automobile business in North America; however, no decisions have been made regarding a new US plant." At least one thing is clear. Honda Civic sales are up 3.3%, CR-V sales are up 6.4%, and Accord sales are up a whopping 32.5% for the year. All these vehicles are built in North America, so if demand continues to rise, Honda may have no choice but to invest in more manufacturing. CarBuzz Insight – Why This Matters: 2026 Honda Accord SE front 3/4 high angle in black while driving Honda Right now, the only thing predictable in the auto industry is that things are largely unpredictable. Political headwinds is a term often tossed around these days, and those headwinds can change day by day, or even hour by hour if something upsets the Trump administration in Washington. But, there is a push for more affordable vehicles and strong sales for Civic, Accord, and CR-V suggest buyers are reconsidering their needs for new family vehicles. The big question is whether that trend will still exist in two or three years – the time it generally takes to get a new plant built and running. Political headwinds will change by then, but if Honda can future-proof its new factory to accommodate multiple scenarios, then there's hardly a downside to expanding in America. Source: Automotive News

records.excerpt: Honda, GAC extend GAC Honda joint venture to 2038 as sales slump - CnEVPost Japanese Auto | Honda Honda, GAC extend GAC Honda joint venture to 2038 as sales slump Phate Zhang • Jul 20, 2026 at 3:30 PM UTC 0 2 + Add us on Google +G Add CnEVPost as your preferred source to stay updated on important EV news. File photo shows a GAC Honda P7 EV. Credit: CnEVPost The two parties extended the term of their GAC Honda joint venture through 2038 while keeping their ownership structure unchanged. GAC Honda has come under mounting sales pressure, with first-half sales falling 55.82% year-on-year. Honda and GAC Group (HKEX: 2238) have signed an agreement to renew their GAC Honda joint venture, extending the partnership through 2038 while keeping their ownership stakes unchanged. Honda China announced the renewal in a statement on Monday, as competition in China's auto market intensifies and joint-venture brands continue to lose market share. Founded in July 1998, GAC Honda was Honda's first joint venture in China responsible for vehicle production and sales. GAC and Honda each hold a 50% stake. records.title: Honda Pivot Continues with Plan for Eighth North American Plant After cancelling its 0 EV project, Honda is considering another North American plant to help grow its hybrid offerin
records.excerpt: Honda plans Eighth North American assembly plant | Car News | Auto123 News Cars for sale Technical Specs Car Guides Car Reviews Our Writers Sell your car Car Releases Auto Shows Top 10 Industry Concept Cars Green Wheels News Honda Pivot Continues with Plan for Eighth North American Plant Honda's Americna HQ, in Torrance, California | Photo: Honda Derek Boshouwers July 20, 2026 After cancelling its 0 EV project, Honda is considering another North American plant to help grow its hybrid offering. Following a strategic retreat from its ambitious all-electric vehicle plans, Honda is preparing to double down on its most profitable market. CEO Toshihiro Mibe recently revealed that the Japanese automaker is planning to build an eighth vehicle assembly plant in North America. Why? For three very good reasons: 1) To boost market share in its most important market; 2) To circumvent potential tariffs that could obstruct its growth in that market; 3) U.S. consumer demand for hybrids and ICE vehicles has soared. How important is North America to Honda? It accounts for somewhere around 40 percent of its global sales. The company currently has seven assembly plants on the continent, including four in the U.S., two in Canada (centered in Alliston, Ontario) and one in Mexico, and they are currently running at 90 percent of their annual 1.8-million-vehicle capacity. “If you don't have a buffer, you can't recover production,” Mibe told Japan’s Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, emphasizing the need for operational wiggle room as Honda targets a U.S. market share beyond its current 9 percent. For Reason Number Two cited above, we can be fairly sure that by North American plant, Honda means a U.S. plant. But we shall see what the future holds. The Honda logo, at the 2025 Chicago Auto Show | Photo: D.Boshouwers Sharp shift in strategy The potential manufacturing expansion follows a massive, multi-billion-dollar 0-shaped pivot. Shifting consumer sentiment and changes to federal tax incentives in the U.S. led Honda to scrap its entire upcoming 0 Series EV lineup. Just recently, the brand discontinued the GM-built Prologue electric SUV after sales plummeted up to 50 percent in the first half of the year. Rather than chasing an electric market that is currently anemic in the U.S., Honda is redirecting its focus toward high-demand hybrid powertrains. Mibe noted that mainstream American buyers are unlikely to adopt EVs fully for at least another five years, making local hybrid production the smarter, more stable play for the short term. | Photo: Honda Made in the USA An eighth facility would further solidify Honda’s massive footprint as a domestic manufacturing powerhouse. The brand already builds 13 models that rank highly on the Cars.com American-Made Index, with its Alabama plant leading the industry in top-10 ranked vehicles. By expanding local assembly, Honda intends to adhere to its core philosophy of building cars where they are sold, while safeguarding its supply chain against volatile import policies. For now, Honda is maintaining that it has not made any definitive decisions regarding a new plant, including where and when it might set up, and even if it will. But it seems very likely to happen, since the automaker's leadership has made it clear that expanding capacity is the definitive next step. records.title: Acura Is Reportedly Planning a New Three-Row SUV Flagship That'll Slot Above the MDX
records.excerpt: Acura is reportedly revisiting a decades-old plan to make a large SUV, but it won't enter production until 2029. Acura is developing a larger three-row SUV that'll sit atop its lineup, according to a report by Automotive News. The new SUV will reportedly offer a lot more third-row legroom and feature the same hybrid powertrain found in the next-generation Acura RDX and Honda Accord.Dubbed the "Acura XL," plans are still in the preliminary phase, and production isn't expected to start until September 2029.In 2008, Acura teased an ambitious plan to introduce five new products to its lineup. Then the financial crisis happened, and the brand's aspirations for a V-8-powered, rear-wheel-drive platform were thrown in the bin. Acura scaled down its five-vehicle proposal and filed away the rest of its notebooks. However, among those scrapped plans, there was reportedly a larger three-row SUV to sit above the mid-size Acura MDX and compete with luxury brands. It's been a long time coming, but Acura could finally resurrect those old plans and bring the large SUV flagship to life, according to a report by Automotive News.This new vehicle, dubbed the "Acura XL" in documents, is expected to be larger than the MDX and compete directly with competitors such as the Buick Enclave and Lexus TX, which both have more third-row legroom than the MDX. The proposed Acura will be equipped with a newly developed hybrid powertrain, per the AN report, which might help it stand out in a crowded segment. Only the TX and Volvo XC90 currently offer a hybrid version, but that could change by the time the "XL" goes on sale near the end of the decade.This is all still in the preliminary phase, though. In the meantime, Acura's lineup will consist of just three models during a two-year break in production of the RDX; we expect the fourth generation to debut in 2028, featuring the new hybrid powertrain and a complete redesign. Honda and Acura gave us our first look at the future powertrain, along with the redesigned Honda Accord and RDX, back in May. At the time, Honda said the new system would slash costs by over 30 percent and improve fuel efficiency by at least 10 percent. Acura reportedly expects to produce around 40,000 copies of the new flagship SUV per year, but it'll be a while before we see it go on sale, as production isn't expected to start until September 2029.➡️ Skip the lot. records.title: Honda extends JV agreement with GAC Group to 2038
records.excerpt: Honda extends JV agreement with GAC Group to 2038 Honda extends JV agreement with GAC Group to 2038 · Just Auto GlobalData Tue, July 21, 2026 at 3:52 AM PDT 2 min read HMC 601238.SS Japanese automaker Honda Motor has announced that it has reached an agreement with Chinese state-owned automaker Guangzhou Automobile Group Company to extend the term of their vehicle production and sales joint venture, GAC Honda Automobile Company Ltd (GAC Honda), through to 2038. Honda holds 50% of the shares in GAC Honda, including 40% held directly and 10% held by its wholly-owned subsidiary Honda Motor (China) Investment Company Ltd, while Guangzhou Automobile Group owns the remaining 50% of the equity. The joint venture was established in 1998, with production at its first vehicle production line in Guangzhou beginning in early 1999. While cumulative production at GAC Honda has exceeded 11 million units since operations first began, the joint venture has failed to keep pace with China's rapid transition to new energy vehicles (NEVs) in recent years. Sales plunged by 53% to 64,150 units in the first half of 2026. Honda said in a statement: "Today, China has grown into the world's largest automobile market in volume, where competition continues to intensify amid the rapid advancement of electrification and intelligent technologies. By fully leveraging the respective technologies and resources of Honda and GAC Group, and continuing to offer products that meet the diverse needs of customers, Honda will further strengthen its automobile business in China." Honda is understood to be planning to restructure its operations in China, which also include a joint venture in Wuhan with Dongfeng Motor Group, called Dongfeng Honda Automobile Company. The two joint ventures have a combined production capacity of 1.2 million vehicles, split between six vehicle assembly plants. According to local reports earlier this year, the company is considering stopping internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle production at GAC Honda and closing down an ICE plant, while stepping up efforts to produce battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for the local and overseas markets. "Honda extends JV agreement with GAC Group to 2038" was originally created and published by Just Auto , a GlobalData owned brand. records.title: Honda announce Aston Martin boost for Hungary ahead of F1 summer break upgrades
records.excerpt: Honda have confirmed that Aston Martin will be bringing a chassis upgrade to this weekend's F1 Hungarian Grand Prix, explaining how they will play a part in ensuring everything goes to plan with it. Honda have confirmed that Aston Martin will be bringing a chassis upgrade to this weekend's F1 Hungarian Grand Prix , explaining how they will play a part in ensuring everything goes to plan with it. The highly anticipated chassis upgrade which Aston Martin have design legend Adrian Newey to thank for has split opinion so far, but this weekend we will finally get to see whether the improvements translate into a boost on track . The Silverstone F1 squad currently sit second from bottom in the constructors' standings thanks to the single point Fernando Alonso has won for them across the first 10 rounds of the campaign, with only Cadillac sat below them. Article continues under video But the unfortunate reality for Aston Martin is that even the brand new American squad have been ahead of them on track for most of this year, with gaps of up to six seconds seen at last weekend's race in Spa. The Belgian GP once again saw neither Alonso nor his team-mate Lance Stroll make it to the finish line , but there is light at the end of the tunnel as Newey's first chassis upgrade is expected to improve their aerodynamic package this weekend. F1 HEADLINES: Red Bull make $3bn decision, Verstappen future takes fresh twist Honda lay out Aston Martin Hungarian GP expectations Ahead of the final race before the annual summer shutdown, Honda's trackside general manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara painted a picture of what fans can expect from Aston Martin given they will only be bringing an upgrade on the chassis side, not the power unit, which is instead coming into play at the first race back in August, the Dutch Grand Prix . "The big talking point for the Hungarian Grand Prix is that the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team will introduce their chassis upgrade," said Orihara in a Honda preview of the Hungarian GP. "We are working closely with them to support on the power unit integration aspects, making FP1 a very important session to check the functionalities." Turning his attention to the specific demands of the Hungarian track, the Japanese engineer added: "The Hungaroring is less sensitive for the power unit so we may be able to expect better performance despite not having our B-spec engine here. "It’s also typically a warm race so we will need to check the cooling elements too at the start of the weekend." The last race before the summer break is here ?? Shintaro Orihara previews the Hungarian Grand Prix: “The big talking point for the Hungarian Grand Prix is that the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One™ Team will introduce their chassis upgrade... pic.twitter.com/gvBzWaoE62 — Honda Racing F1 (@HondaRacingF1) July 21, 2026 When is the F1 Hungarian Grand Prix? Just like last weekend's event in Belgium, the Hungarian GP will follow a traditional schedule, kicking off with FP1 on Friday, July 24 at 13:30 local time (CEST). The track action will continue on Friday evening at 5pm local time. Saturday will begin with the final hour of practice from 12:30 until 13:30 CEST before the first competitive session of the weekend commences with qualifying at 16:00. Lights out for Sunday's Hungarian GP will then take place at 3pm CEST, which is 2pm BST for those tuning in from the UK. records.excerpt: MotoGP News: Honda signs Alonso and Quartararo Skip to content AutoRacing1.com An Inside Look at Motorsports Hot News MotoGP MotoGP News: Honda signs Alonso and Quartararo Posted by AR1 staff July 21, 2026 Two press releases by Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) on their MotoGP riders for 2027 and beyond – Fabio Quartararo (pictured) and David Alonso. Honda Racing Corporation signs Fabio Quartararo Honda Racing Corporation signs Fabio Quartararo Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) are pleased to announce the signing of Fabio Quartararo for the 2027 and 2028 MotoGP World Championship seasons. Quartararo will race for the factory Honda HRC team as the 850cc era of MotoGP begins from 2027. The 27-year-old joined the premier class in 2019 after a record-breaking run in the FIM CEV Moto3 International Championship and four competitive seasons in the Moto3 and Moto2 World Championships. As a rookie in the premier class, Quartararo made his presence known and scored pole position in just his fourth race with a total of six poles and seven podiums in 2019. In 2021 he would take the MotoGP World Championship title, battling to second the following year. The French rider has taken a total of 11 wins, 32 podiums and 21 poles to date in the premier class. Honda Racing Corporation signs David Alonso Honda Racing Corporation signs David Alonso Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) are pleased to confirm the signing of David Alonso on a multi-year contract for the MotoGP World Championship. The 20-year-old Colombian has authored one of the most impressive runs through the lightweight classes in recent times, finishing third as a Moto3 rookie in 2023 before dominating the class the following year. Currently in his second season in the Moto2 World Championship, Alonso took his maiden intermediate class win at the 2025 Hungarian Grand Prix and currently sits fourth overall in the 2026 title hunt. With a total of 20 wins, 30 podiums, and nine pole positions across Moto3 and Moto2, Alonso has continued to surpass expectations. records.excerpt: 2024 Moto3 champion David Alonso signs HRC MotoGP contract MCN Reviews For sale News Insurance MotoGP: David Alonso signs multi-year contract with Honda By Josh Close Follow MCN on Google Add MCN as a preferred source on Google to see more of our latest content Published: Yesterday 11:22 David Alonso will be a MotoGP rider with Honda in 2027. David Alonso in Moto2 action for Aspar at the Sachsenring. David Alonso celebrates becoming 2024 Moto3 world champion at Motegi. 1 of 3 Honda has confirmed the signing of David Alonso for the 2027 MotoGP season however it’s not yet known which Honda team the Colombian will compete for. The 2024 Moto3 world champion has been linked with Honda for the majority of the year, with reports initially suggesting that he would line-up alongside Fabio Quartararo in the factory team. However, in recent weeks, current LCR Honda rider Diogo Moreira has also been linked with a promotion to the factory setup. The Brazilian has impressed so far in his maiden premier class campaign, and it appears HRC bosses are struggling to come to a decision. As for Alonso, he’s signed a multi-year contract with Honda and much is expected of the 20-year-old in the next few years. Known as the ‘Baby GOAT’, Alonso is a former European Talent Cup (2020) and Red Bull Rookies (2021) champion, as well as being crowned the 2024 Moto3 world champion. In his title-winning 2021 campaign, Alonso broke multiple records throughout the season. Riding for the Aspar team, Alonso broke Valentino Rossi’s lightweight class record for wins in a single season (11) by standing on the top step on 14 occasions. Alonso also holds the record for most consecutive wins (7), as well as the most points in a single season (421), the biggest title-winning margin (165) and the most career Moto3 victories (18). He also equalled the record for most podiums in a single season (15). His time in Moto2 hasn’t been as straightforward. Alonso suffered a shoulder injury ahead of pre-season testing in 2025, which put him on the back foot in the opening rounds. Alonso ended his maiden Moto2 campaign ninth overall with one victory and four further podiums. 2026 has been a more consistent campaign so far, with Alonso currently fourth in the championship. Alonso won at Assen and finished second at Brno, whilst he’s finished inside the top six on six further occasions. Alonso will make his debut on the 2027 Honda machine at the post-race Valencia Test. records.label: crash.net
records.title: Honda confirms David Alonso’s 2027 MotoGP signing, but key detail still missing
records.excerpt: Honda confirms David Alonso’s 2027 MotoGP signing, but key detail still missing | Crash.net Skip to main content Log in Honda confirms David Alonso’s 2027 MotoGP signing, but key detail still missing Honda has confirmed it has signed David Alonso for the 2027 MotoGP season Lewis Duncan Updated: 21 Jul 2026 Share David Alonso © Gold and Goose Honda has confirmed it has signed David Alonso to a multi-year factory MotoGP contract for 2027, but has yet to finalise what team he will actually race with. The 2024 Moto3 world champion has long been rumoured to make the jump to MotoGP next year with Honda, with all reports initially claiming he would be going to the factory squad with Fabio Quartararo . But in recent months, those reports have lessened, with it thought Honda is torn between promoting Diogo Moreira from LCR and replacing him with Alonso. David Alonso, Aspar, 2026 Brazil MotoGP © Gold and Goose Honda has seemingly not made a firm decision on this, following the announcement on Tuesday morning that it had signed Alonso, but not where he will race. A full statement read: “Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) are pleased to confirm the signing of David Alonso on a multi-year contract for the MotoGP World Championship. “The 20-year-old Colombian has authored one of the most impressive runs through the lightweight classes in recent times, finishing third as a Moto3 rookie in 2023 before dominating the class the following year. “Currently in his second season in the Moto2 World Championship, Alonso took his maiden intermediate class win at the 2025 Hungarian Grand Prix and currently sits fourth overall in the 2026 title hunt. “With a total of 20 wins, 30 podiums and nine pole positions across Moto3 and Moto2, Alonso has continued to surpass expectations. “He will make his debut on the 2027 Honda machine at the post-race Valencia Test.” Honda indecision holding up Quartararo announcement Honda’s lack of a decision on where both Alonso and Moreira will race in 2027 has held up the long-expected announcement of 2021 world champion Fabio Quartararo joining the brand. Quartararo’s move to Honda’s factory team was first reported before pre-season testing began, as Yamaha failed to convince him to stay put beyond 2026. The Frenchman said at the recent German Grand Prix: “I don't really know when [the announcement will be, exactly, but for sure it’s not going to be super long. Fabio Quartararo. © Gold and Goose “I think [the official announcement] is more for the public or whatever, but I think I have nothing to hide. It's just that I cannot say.” Moreira has been impressive in his debut MotoGP season with LCR, finishing all but two grands prix in the points so far. He has a best finish of sixth at the Hungarian Grand Prix, with the Brazilian 16th in the standings at the summer break. It’s this strong form that has created a headache for Honda in deciding what to do with Alonso, who is currently fourth in the Moto2 points. Until that is resolved, an official announcement on Quartararo’s future remains on hold. As of now, Honda’s factory team is the only one on the grid who hasn’t announced its line-up for 2027. Alonso's Moto2 team-mate Dani Holgado will move to MotoGP with Gresini Ducati next season, while Maximo Quiles will step up to Moto2 with the Aspar squad in his place. records.excerpt: サッカー w杯2026年FIFAワールドカップ（北中米大会）―。日本は、ブラジルに1-2で惜敗した。ブラジル代表にで敗れて大会を終えた。森保一監督が率いる日本代表はサッカー王国ブラジルに対し互角の試合を展開するも最後は高い壁を超えることができなかった。ところが…日本とブラジルが熱戦を繰り広げるなかピッチ上の代表選手井所に日本中を熱狂させた男がいた。NHKのサッカーW杯中継で解説席に陣取った本田圭佑（40）だ。 2026.07.22 # スポーツ # テレビ # サッカー 「日本に最悪のサプライズ」本田圭佑に「韓国代表」監督就任説が急浮上…！W杯で”裏MVP”となった男の「信じがたい未来図」 現代ビジネス編集部 ワールドカップの裏MVPは本田圭佑だった スペインが優勝を飾った、サッカーW杯2026年FIFAワールドカップ（北中米大会）。日本はブラジルに1-2で惜敗して、大会を終えている。 森保一監督が率いる日本代表は、サッカー王国ブラジルに対し互角の試合を展開するも、最後は高い壁を超えることができなかった。一方、日本とブラジルが熱戦を繰り広げるなか、ピッチ上の代表選手以上に日本中を熱狂させた男がいた。NHKのサッカーW杯中継で、解説席に陣取った元日本代表の本田圭佑（40歳）だ。 photo by Gettyimages この記事の全ての写真を見る（全4枚） -AD- 「戦術論にとどまらず、選手の焦りや監督の迷い、勝負所の空気をズバズバ本音で切り取る“本田節”に視聴者は一喜一憂したんです。本田の解説を聞くために、地上波のフジテレビが中継した視聴人数とNHKがほぼ肩を並べるという快挙を成し遂げ、テレビ業界の常識を覆す大番狂わせを演じました。アナウンサー顔負けの予定調和を嫌う本田のナマの言葉に、Z世代を中心とした一般層の心を見事に鷲掴みされましたね。まさに本田劇場だった」（民放キー局編成担当） 日本代表の敗退後、本田はその勢いに乗ったまま、自身のSNSで「僕を1年試して。アジア杯で負ければクビでいい」と配信した。事実上の次期日本代表監督への堂々たる立候補宣言だった。これに対し日本サッカー協会の反応は冷たかった。 関連記事 ゆうちゃみ「お股まで洗ってもらってる」と衝撃発言…！令和ギャルが「風呂キャンセル界隈」になった”驚きの事情” フジテレビが佐藤二朗を「見捨てた」ゾッとする理由…「中居正広騒動」が残した、洒落にならない「トラウマ」とは 大野智に古参ファンが「カネの亡者か！」と”大激怒”…個サロの年会費が「３万円強」になった「白々しいワケ」 ＼現代ビジネスの記事を見つけやすく／ Google検索で優先表示 関連タグ # スポーツ # テレビ # サッカー
